newsitem.title: UK: Hogg says UK is raising meat hygiene standards.
newsitem.headline: Hogg says UK is raising meat hygiene standards.

text.p: Agriculture Minister Douglas Hogg on Wednesday defended his department's record in improving standards of hygiene in Britain's abattoirs and said a work programme was in hand to raise them even further.

In a statement to parliament, Hogg said reports on meat safety circulated in recent days by the opposition Labour party had been misleading because they did not take account of the important progress made over the last 18 months.

"I do not pretend that there is not scope for further improvement. But I can assure the House that the Ministry of Agriculture... and the Meat Hygiene Service (MHS) had been and remained determined to drive up standards and we are succeeding," Hogg said.
He said the MHS, set up by the government in 1995, would apply its hygiene rules ever more strictly.

"Every plant now knows where its weak points are. Plants which are found repeatedly to have low standards will face progressively stricter attention from the mean inspectors and, as I have said, in appropriate cases prosecutions will ensue.
"Our purpose is to bring our abattoir practice up to the highest possible standards," Hogg said.
Hogg was trying to dampen an outcry provoked on Wednesday when Labour produced a letter by Peter Comrie, the Association of Meat Inspectors' general secretary.

Comrie warned that falling standards were creating "a potential timebomb" in Britain's slaughterhouses and said some inspectors had been threatened for trying to take action over breaches of hygiene rules.
Labour's agriculture spokesman, Gavin Strang, demanded the establishment of an independent food standards agency and said Hogg had failed to address the questions raised.
"He is not effectively tackling these problems. There is no confidence in him, nor his government, as far as food safety issues are concerned," Strang said.
Paul Marland, a farmer and Conservative member of parliament's agriculture committee, accused Labour of "blatant opportunism" in the run-up to the election.
Hogg agreed and said Labour's "irresponsible scaremongering" would damage not only Britain's meat industry but also the country's standing in Europe.
"The fact that it's hysterical, irresponsible and ill-informed will not be understood in Europe. They will simply treat it at face value," Hogg said.
